records.text: Candace Owens cited a 2012 Los Angeles Times report that Bain Capital sought an initial $37 million fund and Robert Maxwell contributed $2 million.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Apparently, the Los Angeles Times did a piece uncovering this back in 2012. When Mitt Romney was running, they learned that he was struggling to raise the initial $37 million that they wanted for their fund. So they turned to foreign investors and Robert Maxwell gave him $2 million out of the $37 million, as well as some other foreign shady investors.

verification.notes: The cited July 19, 2012 Los Angeles Times report says Bain raised its first $37 million investment fund and that Robert Maxwell was an early investor who contributed $2 million. The citation accurately represents the article.

sources.title: Bain Capital started with help of offshore investors
sources.relevance: The cited article directly states the first fund amount and Maxwell investment.

records.text: Mitt Romney founded Bain Capital with Robert Maxwell, whom Candace Owens described as an Israeli spy, as one of its seed investors.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now, I'm going to remind you also that from the Boston Consulting Group, Mitt Romney founded Bain Capital with an Israeli spy. ... Robert Maxwell, Ghislaine Maxwell's father, as one of his seed investors.

verification.notes: Robert Maxwell was an early outside investor in Bain Capital’s first fund, but Bain partners supplied the initial capital and reliable reporting does not establish him as the singular seed investor. His intelligence ties are long alleged and disputed; describing him categorically as an Israeli spy overstates the public evidence.

sources.title: Attempt to link Mitt Romney to alleged spy Robert Maxwell is misleading
sources.relevance: Documents Maxwell as an early Bain fund investor while distinguishing him from Bain’s initial seed capital.

sources.title: The mystery of Maxwell’s death
sources.relevance: Reviews competing allegations and evidence concerning Maxwell’s relationships with intelligence services.

records.text: Owens said Frank William Gay son Robert C. Gay served as a managing director of Mitt Romney Bain Capital for 16 years.

appearances.snippet: I should also mention that Frank William Gay, the trusted Mormon, he had a son, Robert Gay, who became the managing director of Mitt Romney's Bain Capital for 16 years.

verification.notes: The University of Utah biography identifies Robert C. Gay as Frank William Gay's son and records his Bain Capital managing-director service from 1989 through 2004, conventionally described as sixteen years.
